out.caption: Average input, cache, and output tokens per task

notes.title: Input Tokens
paras: Non-cached input tokens sent to the model, including prompts, instructions, tool context, and task context that were not served from prompt cache.
notes.html: Non-cached input tokens sent to the model, including prompts, instructions, tool context, and task context that were not served from prompt cache.

notes.title: Cached Input Tokens
paras: Reused prompt tokens billed through provider prompt caching when that telemetry is available, rather than being processed as a fully fresh input each time.
notes.html: Reused prompt tokens billed through provider prompt caching when that telemetry is available, rather than being processed as a fully fresh input each time.

notes.title: Why Cache Usage Varies
paras: Some providers route repeated requests across different backend replicas. When prompt cache state is not shared consistently across those replicas, a model may receive fewer cache hits even when the benchmark task flow is otherwise identical.

We do not add custom relay headers or provider-specific affinity controls to force higher cache reuse, because that would make the benchmark less representative of a typical user setup. As a result, reported costs reflect the cache behavior observed through the configured provider path, not an optimized best-case cache scenario.
notes.html:

out.caption: Average pay-per-token API cost per task (USD) · Lower is better

notes.title: What Cost Is Measuring
paras: This chart shows the average pay-per-token API cost per task across the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, spanning DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench v2, and SWE-Atlas-QnA.

Where applicable, that cost model includes standard input pricing, discounted cached-input pricing, separate cache-write charges, and output pricing rather than treating all prompt tokens as if they were billed at the same uncached input rate.

It is intended to show pay-per-token API cost, not consumer plan pricing or the full operational cost of deploying the system in production. Infrastructure, engineering, and supervision costs are not the focus of this metric.
